title: Turn a customer kickoff into the requirements specification for a river-level logger
person: An electronics engineer at a small instrument maker writing the requirements for a new logger after the customer kickoff.
review: Level 0 m to 5 m within ± 5 mm, water temperature −5 °C to 35 °C within ± 0.2 °C, a reading every 15 min, at least one year of readings stored, one upload a day, 10 m submersion for 72 h, at most 2 kg with batteries, a 50 mm pole mount, operation from −20 °C to 50 °C; the 18-month battery life is a TBR for Priya Raman by 30 November 2026.
revised_review: Readings every 10 min everywhere, and a new requirement for a level-rise alarm within 5 min of a rise of more than 0.5 m in an hour; nothing else changed.

criteria.text: Every mechanical check in run.py passes for this stage.
Every requirement has an id of its own, used once.
Requirements say shall, facts will and goals should; nothing says must.
No vague word from the notes survives into a requirement.
Every TBD or TBR has an owner and a date.
Every requirement names test, analysis, inspection or demonstration.
Every value has a space before its unit symbol, °C and % included.
The notes' unit spellings are replaced by the SI symbols.
The 18-month battery life is a best estimate marked TBR, owned by Priya Raman and due by 30 November 2026.
The level and temperature requirements carry their ± tolerances.
Every need in the notes is a requirement or a goal with its value, and nothing is invented.
The interval is 10 min everywhere and the rise alarm is a new requirement with its own id; nothing else changed.

source: Synthetic material created for this evaluation pack; the companies, schools and people are invented.
stage_policy: Separate first and revision directories; reveal revision only after first output is frozen.
